root_cause: The keyboard navigation (ArrowRight/ArrowLeft) in Pikaday's `_onKeyChange` calls `adjustDate` which moves by exactly one day without checking if the target day is disabled (e.g., weekends). This causes the selection to land on a disabled weekend day (Saturday) instead of skipping to the next enabled day (Monday).
repair_strategy: Modify the `adjustDate` method to iterate day-by-day in the same direction until it finds a date that is not disabled (respecting minDate, maxDate, disableWeekends, and disableDayFn). This ensures all keyboard navigation (including up/down) never lands on a disabled day.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate the date picker with arrow keys without landing on disabled weekend dates, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard), 2.4.3 (Focus Order), and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
functional_risks: Week navigation (up/down) may move more than 7 days if the target day is disabled, but will always land on an enabled day.
Infinite loop protection via maxIterations (365) prevents runaway loops if all days are disabled.
verification_requirements: ArrowRight from Friday 2026-11-20 selects Monday 2026-11-23 (skipping weekend).
Up/Down arrow keys move by week and skip disabled days if necessary.
Min/max date boundaries and custom disableDayFn are respected.
